breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article V. Employee Benefits > § 56-5.7. Retirement; deferred compensation plan.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article V. Employee Benefits > § 56-5.7. Retirement; deferred compensation plan.

*[Amended 5-20-2025 by Ord. No. 101-2025]*

The City offers regular, full-time employees the benefit of a Section 457 deferred compensation plan. Participation is voluntary and allows qualifying employees the option of deferring a portion of their salary to be invested by the plan administrators. Employees may defer the maximum allowed under the IRS rules and regulations, as may be amended. The maximum amount includes both the employee and employer contributions.

- A. Eligibility requirements. Regular, full-time employees of the City of Waterville are eligible to enroll in the deferred compensation plan upon date of hire; however, the City contribution will not begin until the employee has completed one full year of continuous employment. A participation agreement must be signed to defer actual receipt of portions of salary not yet earned by having the deferred amount contributed to this plan rather than paid as regular earnings. Participation agreements may be made at any time and will take effect the next possible payroll period unless the employee specifies a different beginning date. Employees must elect to defer a minimum of $25 per month to participate in the plan.

- B. Contribution.

  - (1) The City will contribute an amount equal to 5% of the employee's base compensation when the employee contributes 3%, and 7% when the employee contributes 5%. The employee contribution is immediately vested at 100%. City contributions will not begin until the employee has completed one year of service.

  - (2) Employees enrolled in MainePERS are not eligible for any City contributions.

- C. Vesting schedule. The City contribution will be vested in the plan according to the following schedule:

| Years of Employment | Vesting Percentage |
| --- | --- |
| After 1 | 20% |
| After 2 | 40% |
| After 3 | 60% |
| After 4 | 80% |
| After 5 | 100% |

- D. Roth IRA. Regular, full time employees of the City are eligible to enroll in a Roth IRA through MissionSquare Retirement. The City will not contribute any funds to this plan for employees. A participation application and agreement must be signed and approved by MissionSquare Retirement before an employee can contribute to the plan. Participation agreements may be made at any time and will take effect the next possible payroll period after the City has received confirmation of the account approval from MissionSquare Retirement.
title: § 56-5.7. Retirement; deferred compensation plan.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article V. Employee Benefits > § 56-5.8. Unemployment compensation.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article V. Employee Benefits > § 56-5.8. Unemployment compensation.

*[Amended 5-20-2025 by Ord. No. 101-2025]*

Under provisions of law, employees whose jobs are lost through no fault of their own may receive an allowance from the Bureau of Unemployment Compensation while unemployed and seeking employment. Employees or former employees who have questions regarding eligibility are advised to contact the Maine Department of Labor.
title: § 56-5.8. Unemployment compensation.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article V. Employee Benefits > § 56-5.9. Worker's compensation.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article V. Employee Benefits > § 56-5.9. Worker's compensation.

- A. Workers' compensation benefits are governed by state law. All job-related injuries shall be immediately reported to the employee's immediate supervisor, who shall, with the employee's assistance, complete and submit the first report of injury form and follow the steps as outlined in the City's Workers' Compensation Policy. Eligible employees will receive workers' compensation benefits as established by state law.

- B. If a workers' compensation claim is disputed by the insurance carrier, time lost will be charged to sick leave or other available earned leave. Should the employee prevail in any disputed days, such leave charged will be credited according to guidelines established by the rules and regulations of the Workers' Compensation Board.
title: § 56-5.9. Worker's compensation.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article V. Employee Benefits > § 56-5.10. Employee wellness.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article V. Employee Benefits > § 56-5.10. Employee wellness.

- A. The City encourages the health and fitness of all City employees. To this end, the City supports the work of the Wellness Committee in scheduling programs for employees.

- B. The City will reimburse regular, full-time employees with active memberships at area health facilities a portion of the annual membership cost.
title: § 56-5.10. Employee wellness.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article V. Employee Benefits > § 56-5.11. Employee Assistance Program.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article V. Employee Benefits > § 56-5.11. Employee Assistance Program.

All employees are eligible to participate in the Employee Assistance Program. The program is designed to restore valuable employees to full productivity. The program provides assessment and referral services to employees who are experiencing on-the-job problems because of job-related or personal difficulties, including substance abuse, family difficulties, emotional, financial or legal worries which result in a decline of job performance. Participation in the program is voluntary and strictly confidential. Contact the Human Resources Office or your supervisor for additional information.
title: § 56-5.11. Employee Assistance Program.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article V. Employee Benefits > § 56-5.12. Vehicle allowance.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article V. Employee Benefits > § 56-5.12. Vehicle allowance.

Employees who are required by the nature of their positions to have a vehicle available 24 hours per day, seven days per week, or employees who are required to use their personal vehicles during the greater part of their working hours, may receive a vehicle allowance. As a general rule, this provision applies to department heads and specialized professional staff as determined by the City Manager. The amount of the monthly vehicle allowance will be determined by the City Manager.
title: § 56-5.12. Vehicle allowance.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article V. Employee Benefits > § 56-5.13. Mileage reimbursement.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article V. Employee Benefits > § 56-5.13. Mileage reimbursement.

*[Amended 5-20-2025 by Ord. No. 101-2025]*

- A. Reimbursements to employees who may use their personal vehicle for conducting City business will be at the current IRS standard mileage rate. Employees will not be reimbursed for nonbusiness purposes, including, but not limited to, the following:

  - (1) Mileage to and from residence;

  - (2) Mileage for personal business;

  - (3) Mileage to and from lunch unless conducting City business or attending an approved training session.

- B. Employees are responsible for submitting a record of the mileage to their immediate supervisor for review and approval. Mileage will be reimbursed through the payroll process.

- C. City employees who receive a vehicle allowance are not entitled to mileage reimbursement for travel within the Greater Waterville Area. Travel outside the Greater Waterville Area will be reimbursed at a rate determined by the City Manager. (The Greater Waterville Area encompasses a twenty-five mile radius.)
title: § 56-5.13. Mileage reimbursement.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article V. Employee Benefits > § 56-5.14. Travel policy.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article V. Employee Benefits > § 56-5.14. Travel policy.

*[Amended 5-20-2025 by Ord. No. 101-2025]*

- A. The City shall reimburse employees for travel expenses that are preapproved, reasonable and directly job-related. All travel outside the Greater Waterville Area must be authorized by the City Manager or his/her designee. (The Greater Waterville Area encompasses a twenty-five-mile radius.)

- B. Breakfast expenses incurred outside the Greater Waterville Area will not be reimbursed unless the trip commences before 7:00 a.m. Dinner expenses incurred outside the Greater Waterville Area will not be reimbursed unless the trip concludes after 7:00 p.m.

- C. Prepayment of travel expenses will be allowed with appropriate documentation. When the employee returns, the employee will provide actual receipts to prove expenses. Employees will be required to repay any amount not accounted for as a proper expense. If the amount prepaid exceeds the actual paid, the employee will reimburse the City the difference. If the amount prepaid is less than actual paid, the City will pay the employee the difference.
title: § 56-5.14. Travel policy.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article V. Employee Benefits > § 56-5.15. Income protection plan.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article V. Employee Benefits > § 56-5.15. Income protection plan.

- A. Regular, full time employees have the opportunity to participate in an income protection plan through the Maine Municipal Association. Each employee has the opportunity to choose to protect 40%, 55% or 70% of the employee's base salary. Employees are required to pay 100% of the entire premium for this coverage.

- B. Employees are eligible for the weekly disability insurance as outlined above when the inability to work is not work-related.

- C. Employees receiving the benefit have two options:

  - (1) Receiving the entire amount of the disability benefit and 100% of their accumulated sick leave (i.e., 70% IPP and 100% sick pay); or

  - (2) Receiving a combination of the entire amount of the disability benefit and a reduced amount of accumulated sick leave pay to bring them up to 100% of their base pay (i.e., 70% IPP and 30% sick pay).

- D. Employees must notify the Human Resource Officer and department head in writing at the time disability leave begins which option they wish to utilize. If nothing is received in writing, Option (1) will be utilized. An employee must have sick and/or vacation time and be receiving a paycheck from the City in order to continue all other benefits as currently available to employees.
title: § 56-5.15. Income protection plan.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article V. Employee Benefits > § 56-5.16. Medical and dependent care reimbursement accounts.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article V. Employee Benefits > § 56-5.16. Medical and dependent care reimbursement accounts.

- A. A reimbursement account is a way for you to put money aside tax-free to be reimbursed to you when you have eligible medical and dependent care expenses. You elect an annual amount that will be withheld from your paycheck in equal installments over the course of the plan year.

- B. Regular, full-time employees may sign up during an open enrollment period for each plan year, which runs from January to December. Termination of the account becomes effective the date of termination from employment from the City.

- C. Please see the Human Resource Officer for handouts explaining the accounts in greater detail and to receive enrollment forms.
section_title: Medical and dependent care reimbursement accounts.
title: § 56-5.16. Medical and dependent care reimbursement accounts.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.1. Sick leave eligibility and accrual.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.1. Sick leave eligibility and accrual.

*[Amended 12-3-2024 by Ord. No. 227-2024; 12-2-2025 by Ord. No. 219-2025]*

- A. Accrual rates.

  - (1) Regular, full-time employees working a four-day work week shall accrue sick leave from the date of hire at a rate of 12.5 hours (1.25 days) per month and may accumulate unused sick leave to a maximum of 1,200 hours (120 days). Sick leave will be credited on the last paycheck of the month.

  - (2) Regular, full-time employees working a five-day work week shall accrue sick leave from the date of hire at a rate of 10 hours (1.25 days) per month and may accumulate unused sick leave to a maximum of 960 hours (120 days). Sick leave will be credited on the last paycheck of the month.

- B. No employee will be eligible for paid sick leave unless accrued.

- C. Sick leave credits shall not be earned by an employee during a leave of absence without pay, a suspension without pay or when the employee is otherwise in a non-pay status.
title: § 56-6.1. Sick leave eligibility and accrual.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.2. Use of sick leave.
title: § 56-6.2. Use of sick leave.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.3. Sick leave requests.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.3. Sick leave requests.

- A. The employee is responsible for notifying the immediate supervisor or department head of the need to use sick leave. Sick leave will be granted only if the employee notifies the appropriate authority prior to the start of their scheduled workday, or as soon as practical thereafter.

- B. Sick leave granted shall be recorded on the weekly payroll records of the department and accurately recorded with the Finance Office. The immediate supervisor or department head is responsible for ensuring that all sick time is accurately reflected on the weekly time records. The Human Resource Officer shall review and monitor such leave records and investigate cases that raise questions of eligibility or abuse.
title: § 56-6.3. Sick leave requests.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.4. Sick leave entitlement upon separation.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.4. Sick leave entitlement upon separation.

- A. All sick leave accruals shall be forfeited upon separation from City service.

- B. Employees hired prior to January 1, 1986. Employees hired prior to January 1, 1986, may either receive monetary value or early retirement for the full amount of their accumulated sick leave, up to the maximum of 120 days. Dismissals and resignations do not qualify for this provision. See § 56-11.2F.
title: § 56-6.4. Sick leave entitlement upon separation.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.5. Sick leave bank.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.5. Sick leave bank.

In cases of serious illness, an employee may not have sufficient accrued sick time to cover the recovery period. In such cases, the Human Resource Officer may, with the approval of the City Manager, establish a special sick leave bank for the employee which would allow City employees to donate accrued vacation time to the bank for use by the ill employee. As a general rule, the leave bank may not exceed 20 working days. Computation of the days donated will be made on a day-for-a-day basis unless another arrangement has been approved by the City Manager.
title: § 56-6.5. Sick leave bank.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.6. Vacation leave.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.6. Vacation leave.

All regular, full-time employees of the City of Waterville shall be granted vacation leave on the basis of time earned or accrued.

- A. Accrual schedule.

| Years of Service | Vacation Days Granted |
| --- | --- |
| 0 - 5 years | 10 |
| After 5 years | 12 |
| After 6 years | 14 |
| After 7 years | 15 |
| After 11 years | 16 |
| After 12 years | 17 |
| After 13 years | 18 |
| After 14 years | 20 |
| After 15 years | 21 |
| After 16 years | 22 |
| After 17 years | 23 |
| After 18 years | 24 |
| After 19 years | 25 |
| After 24 years | 27 |
| After 29 years | 30 |

  - (1) Employees will begin accruing vacation leave upon date of hire but may not use accumulated vacation leave until completion of their probationary period. Increases in the accrual rate will become effective upon the employee's anniversary date of hire.

  - (2) Employees are strongly encouraged to take vacation leave on an annual basis to maintain high levels of job performance. Employees may accumulate up to a maximum of 150% of their accrual rate. When the maximum accumulation has been reached, the employee shall forfeit any right to additional accrual until the vacation leave is taken. (Only in cases of unforeseen, special circumstances shall the City Manager grant the accrual of vacation time above the maximum of 150%.)

  - (3) It is the responsibility of each employee to be aware of his/her accumulated vacation leave. No employee will receive payment in lieu of annual leave other than upon separation from City employment (except in cases of unforeseen, special circumstances as may be granted by the City Manager).

  - (4) An employee whose position is changed from one department to another in City service shall retain the vacation leave they have accumulated over the year. Employees who separate from City service and are rehired at a later date shall begin accruing at the minimum rate.

  - (5) Employees shall not accrue vacation leave during a leave of absence without pay, a suspension without pay or when the employee is otherwise in a non-pay status.

- B. Requesting vacation leave.

  - (1) Employees must receive prior approval from their department head for requested vacation leave. Such requests may be denied if, in the opinion of the City Manager and/or department head, it shall create a hardship upon departmental and/or City operations. The City Manager or department head may not deny or postpone requested vacation leave for more than six months because of the impact said vacation may have on operations.

  - (2) Employees shall submit a written request for vacation leave as far in advance as possible to allow for sufficient planning of department operations and staff coverage. See § 56-6.7, Earned paid leave, for more information.

- C. Vacation upon separation. Payment for unused, accrued vacation time, up to the maximum allowed, shall be made in the final paycheck at the time of separation.
title: § 56-6.6. Vacation leave.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.7. Earned paid leave.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.7. Earned paid leave. (part 1 of 2)

*[Amended 5-20-2025 by Ord. No. 101-2025; 12-2-2025 by Ord. No. 219-2025]*

Effective January 1, 2021, the City is required to provide up to 40 hours of earned paid leave in a year to covered employees, in accordance with State of Maine law, 26 M.R.S. § 637.

- A. Covered employees.

  - (1) All City employees are considered covered employees under earned paid leave with the following exceptions:

    - (a) Elected municipal officers.

    - (b) Board/Commission members.

    - (c) Summer recreation pool staff.

      - [1] Hours worked during the approved season as defined by the Maine Department of Labor, Bureau of Unemployment Compensation, are not reportable and therefore are not considered eligible towards earned paid leave accruals. These hours worked do count towards the 120 days of employment required for use of any EPL earned outside of the approved season.

      - [2] Hours worked outside of the approved season are considered reportable hours and would be eligible for earned paid leave.

    - (d) Election workers.

      - [1] If the employee is paid less than $1,000 in a calendar year, the individual is not considered a covered employee and therefore is not eligible for earned paid leave. See 26 M.R.S. § 1043(11)(F)(17)(i).

      - [2] If the employee is paid $1,000 or more in a calendar year, the individual is considered a covered employee and therefore would be entitled to earned paid leave.

    - (e) Unpaid volunteers.

  - (2) Union employees. Employees currently covered under a collective bargaining agreement are not covered under this section of the Personnel Ordinance or eligible for earned paid leave. Union employees will continue to follow their respective collective bargaining agreements until the expiration of the agreement. Any contract negotiated after January 1, 2021, will include earned paid leave.

- B. Accrual rate. Employees are entitled to earn one hour of paid leave for every 40 hours worked, up to 40 hours in one year of employment.

  - (1) Full-time employees.

    - (a) Full-time nonunion employees accrue more vacation and sick leave per year than is required under the regulations of the EPL law. See § 56-6.6 for vacation accrual amounts and § 56-6.1 for sick accrual amounts.

    - (b) The first 40 hours of accrued vacation or sick leave used each fiscal year will be considered EPL for all full-time nonunion employees.

  - (2) Part-time and per-diem employees.

    - (a) Part-time and per-diem employees will earn one hour for every 40 hours worked, up to a maximum of 40 hours in one year.

    - (b) The maximum accrual is 40 hours in one year. The City will be utilizing the fiscal year as the year for all EPL balances. Any unused EPL on July 1 of each year will be carried over into the next year.

- C. Use of earned paid leave. An employee may begin using accrued EPL after 120 days of employment. EPL will be paid at the employee's rate of pay as established in the week immediately prior to taking the EPL in accordance with the Department of Labor. EPL can be used for any purpose; however, the following notification for use is required.
title: § 56-6.7. Earned paid leave.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.7. Earned paid leave.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.7. Earned paid leave. (part 2 of 2)

- C. Use of earned paid leave. An employee may begin using accrued EPL after 120 days of employment. EPL will be paid at the employee's rate of pay as established in the week immediately prior to taking the EPL in accordance with the Department of Labor. EPL can be used for any purpose; however, the following notification for use is required.

  - (1) Unforeseen emergency. An employee taking EPL for an emergency, illness, or other sudden necessity where advance notice may not be feasible, must give notice to the department head and/or supervisor as soon as practicable. An emergency or sudden necessity under the EPL is defined as anything within reason that is unforeseen and requires the employee to interrupt their work schedule. This includes care for a person not related to the employee. Written documentation may not be required unless EPL is used over three days, but employees are required to provide a general description of the need for leave time. For example: illness of a child; illness of a day-care provider; transportation issue.

  - (2) Planned leave.

    - (a) An employee taking EPL for planned leave, whether it be for an appointment, personal day or vacation, shall provide at least three weeks' prior notice to the department head of their intent to use their EPL. Department heads may waive the three-week notice if approval of the leave will not interfere with the overall operations of the department.

    - (b) Full-time nonunion employees will follow this notification requirement for the first 40 hours of accrued vacation leave each fiscal year. After that, notification will follow § 56-6.6B.

  - (3) Denial of EPL use. Department heads may deny employees time off, other than for an emergency, illness or sudden necessity. The department head can also restrict dates that such time off may be granted. Examples of department hardship may include department staffing, events, disasters or weather emergencies. This is not an all-inclusive list. The department head can deny a requested date of use if it significantly impacts departmental operations.

- D. Discipline. An employee shall not be disciplined for unscheduled absences when using earned paid leave unless the employee does not follow the notification requirements in Subsection C of this section.

- E. Balance carryover. Unused EPL will be handled as follows:

  - (1) Full-time employees. Full-time nonunion employees will refer to § 56-6.6 of the Personnel Ordinance for carryover requirements.

  - (2) Part-time employees.

    - (a) Any unused EPL balance from the previous fiscal year will be carried forward each July 1.

- F. Separation of employment. Any unused EPL at time of separation will be handled as follows:

  - (1) Full-time employees. Full-time nonunion employees will refer to § 56-6.6C of the Personnel Ordinance for vacation pay at separation.

  - (2) Part-time employees.

    - (a) EPL does not have a cash value and will not be paid out at termination of employment for part-time employees. Any part-time employee who returns to work for the City within a one-year period from the last day of previous employment will have any unused EPL balance reinstated.

    - (b) Example: A part-time employee leaves employment on November 15 due to the end of the fall season and has 14 hours of EPL still available. The employee is not paid the 14 hours of EPL. The employee returns on April 14 of the following year for the start of the spring season. The employee is credited 14 hours of EPL. The employee can continue to accrue and use EPL as stated in this policy.
title: § 56-6.7. Earned paid leave.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.8. Childbirth and pregnancy.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.8. Childbirth and pregnancy.

Childbirth and pregnancy are treated as a temporary disability just as any other non-job-related temporary illness or disability. Employees may use accrued sick leave. (See § 56-6.10, Family medical leave.)
title: § 56-6.8. Childbirth and pregnancy.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.9. Paternity leave.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.9. Paternity leave.

- A. The City of Waterville agrees to grant up to two weeks of paid sick leave, from the birth of the child, for paternity leave after a request is presented in writing to the Human Resources Office, provided the employee has sufficient accumulated sick leave.

- B. Any additional time requested must be reviewed to determine if it qualifies for sick time, or if vacation and/or comp time, if available, will be utilized. In order for additional sick time to be granted, a certificate of illness needs to be presented to the Human Resources Office from the employee's spouse's physician stating that she needs the employee's assistance due to a short-term disability related to the birth of the child.

- C. All time used for paternity leave will be subject to the Family and Medical Leave Act. An employee must meet the requirements of the FMLA to qualify for paid paternity leave. (See § 56-6.10 for requirements.) Any employee may request the use of unpaid leave or use accrued vacation leave if he does not qualify for FMLA or does not have any accumulated time in his leave bank.
title: § 56-6.9. Paternity leave.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.10. Family medical leave.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.10. Family medical leave.

*[Amended 5-20-2025 by Ord. No. 101-2025]*

- A. City employees are covered under the Family Medical Leave Act (FMLA) of 1993, as amended, which allows unpaid leave in the case of serious illness of the employee, the employee's child, spouse or parent, the birth or adoption of a child, or exigency for a spouse, son, daughter or parent on active duty. (See § 56-6.12B.)

- B. Employees are eligible if they have worked a minimum of 1,250 hours over the previous 12 months. The 12 months of employment are not required to be consecutive in order for the employee to qualify for FMLA. The 1,250 hours include only hours actually worked for the employer. Paid leave and unpaid leave, including FMLA leave, are not included in the 1,250-hour requirement.

- C. Upon request, up to 12 weeks of leave shall be granted for qualifying reasons during the twelve-month benefit year. The City uses the twelve-month "rolling" backward method for calculating the benefit year.

- D. Employees may utilize sick leave for immediate family members (spouse, children, parent) that live within the employee's household. Employees may utilize vacation, convenience or unpaid leave to care for immediate family members not living within the employee's household, in accordance with the FMLA.

- E. See the Family and Medical Leave Act in Appendix C.[^1] Contact the Human Resources Office for additional information.

[^1]: Editor's Note: Appendix C is included as an attachment to this chapter.
title: § 56-6.10. Family medical leave.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.11. Bereavement leave.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.11. Bereavement leave.

- A. In the event of a death occurring in the immediate family of an employee, the employee shall, upon request, be granted three days of paid leave. Immediate family is limited to: spouse, registered domestic partner, children, parents, siblings, grandparents and grandchildren, whether by natural heritage or law (in-law). In the event of the death of the employee's spouse, registered domestic partner, child or parent, the employee shall, upon request, be granted two additional days of paid bereavement leave. Any additional time shall be with the approval of the department head and the use of accrued vacation leave.

- B. City employees shall, upon request, be granted up to one day of paid leave to attend the funeral of an aunt, uncle, niece or nephew.

- C. Attendance at the funeral of friends or other family relatives shall be with the approval of the department head and the use of accrued vacation leave.
title: § 56-6.11. Bereavement leave.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.12. Military and exigency leave.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.12. Military and exigency leave.

- A. Military leave.

  - (1) Leave without pay will be granted to employees for purposes of fulfilling military reserve obligations. All requests for military leave must be accompanied by signed orders from the employee's military commander.

  - (2) All requests for military leave must be within one week after the employee receives his/her orders to report to duty and must be approved by the City Manager.

- B. Exigency leave. The City will grant an eligible employee up to a total of 12 work weeks of unpaid leave during the normal twelve-month period established by the employer for FMLA leave for qualifying exigencies arising out of the fact that the employee's spouse, son, daughter or parent is on active duty, or has been notified of an impending call or order of active duty, in support of a contingency operation. This is available for a family member of a military member in the National Guard or Reserves; it does not extend to family members of military members in the Regular Armed Forces.

- C. Military family leave entitlements. An eligible City employee who is a spouse, son, daughter, parent or next of kin of a covered service member with a serious injury or illness will be granted up to 26 work weeks of unpaid leave during a "single twelve-month period" to care for the service member. A covered service member is a current member of the Armed Forces, including a member of the National Guard or Reserves, who is undergoing medical treatment, recuperation or therapy, is otherwise in outpatient status, or is otherwise on the temporary disability retired list, for a serious injury or illness. A serious injury or illness is one that was incurred by a service member in the line of duty on active duty that may render the service member medically unfit to perform the duties of his or her office, grade, rank or rating. The "single twelve-month period" for leave to care for a covered service member with a serious injury or illness begins on the first day the employee takes leave for this reason and ends 12 months later, regardless of the twelve-month period established by the employer for other types of FMLA leave.
title: § 56-6.12. Military and exigency leave.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.13. Jury leave.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.13. Jury leave.

An employee who is required to participate in jury duty will receive his/her regular pay. Jury pay received shall be remitted to the City. Employees shall notify their immediate supervisor or department head as soon as it becomes known that they may be required to serve.
title: § 56-6.13. Jury leave.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.14. Leave without pay.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.14. Leave without pay.

- A. Leave without pay shall be granted by the City Manager only when it is in the best interest of the City to do so. Request for a leave without pay must be approved prior to taking of such leave.

- B. Unpaid leave for other than health-related reasons shall only be granted upon the exhaustion of all accrued vacation leave and may not exceed six months.

- C. Unpaid leave for health-related reasons shall only be granted upon the exhaustion of accrued sick, vacation and compensatory leave and may not exceed six months. When such leave is requested as an extension of sick leave, an acceptable physician's certificate shall be required.

- D. A return to work earlier than the scheduled termination of leave date may be arranged by the supervisor and the employee with the approval of the City Manager. Employees returning to work from an unpaid sick leave shall provide a physician's statement certifying fitness to return.

- E. Employees on an unpaid leave of absence from the City may not be employed elsewhere.

- F. If an employee is unable to return to work on the date stipulated, he/she may submit a written request to extend his/her leave of absence, not to exceed the six-month maximum, subject to the approval of the City Manager. If, on the date following the expiration of the leave of absence, an extension is not requested and granted, and the employee has not returned to his/her position, the employee shall be considered to have resigned from City employment.

- G. All employer-paid benefits cease during an unpaid leave. Employees do not accrue vacation or sick leave and are responsible for the full cost of benefits during the period of unpaid leave.

- H. Short-term unpaid leave. A leave of absence without pay for periods of less than three days may be approved by the appropriate department head. During periods of such leave, employees shall continue to accrue all benefits.
title: § 56-6.14. Leave without pay.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.15. Family Sick Leave Act.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.15. Family Sick Leave Act.

Sick leave may be used when it is necessary to care for immediate family members (spouse, children, or parent) not living within the employee's household, in accordance with the Family Sick Leave Act.
title: § 56-6.15. Family Sick Leave Act.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.16. Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave Act ( PFML).
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VI. Leaves > § 56-6.16. Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave Act ( PFML).

*[Added 12-2-2025 by Ord. No. 219-2025]*

The City Of Waterville will take whatever action necessary to comply with the new Maine Paid Family Medical Leave Act. The City and employees will share the cost of the premiums equally.
section_title: Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave Act ( PFML).
title: § 56-6.16. Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave Act ( PFML).

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VII. Conditions of Employment > § 56-7.1. General policy.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VII. Conditions of Employment > § 56-7.1. General policy.

The City maintains the right to establish the hours of work required for conducting the business operations of all City departments. All officers and employees of the City shall serve the hours required for their respective departments.
title: § 56-7.1. General policy.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VII. Conditions of Employment > § 56-7.2. Standard work hours.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VII. Conditions of Employment > § 56-7.2. Standard work hours.

*[Amended 12-3-2024 by Ord. No. 227-2024]*

- A. Employees will work a standard four-day work week unless hired on a different schedule.

- B. City Hall offices will be open to the public Monday through Thursday, 7:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Departments located outside of City Hall may have other established hours of operation; however, offices will be open to the public Monday through Thursday. Departments outside of City Hall may opt to be open to the public on Friday with approval of the City Manager.

- C. Employees shall work a ten-hour block of time and have a 1/2-hour paid lunch period. Within departments, lunches will be scheduled to ensure adequate staffing to provide services to Waterville citizens throughout the work day when possible.
title: § 56-7.2. Standard work hours.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VII. Conditions of Employment > § 56-7.3. Fair Labor Standards Act exemptions.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VII. Conditions of Employment > § 56-7.3. Fair Labor Standards Act exemptions.

- A. The Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) requires employees be paid minimum wage and overtime, unless they are exempt. Exempt employees are classified as executive/management, administrative, professional, outside sales and computer specialists and must meet minimum salary requirements under the FLSA.

- B. Exempt employees are expected to work the number of hours necessary to meet the requirements of the position and are not entitled to overtime wages as established by the Fair Labor Standards Act. The following positions will be considered exempt from the minimum wage and overtime provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act:

  - (1) City Manager.

  - (2) All department heads.

  - (3) All employees meeting the requirements of the Fair Labor Standards Act.
title: § 56-7.3. Fair Labor Standards Act exemptions.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VII. Conditions of Employment > § 56-7.4. Overtime pay.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VII. Conditions of Employment > § 56-7.4. Overtime pay.

- A. In accordance with applicable laws, hours worked over the normal work week of 40 hours by nonexempt employees shall be paid at the rate of time and one-half the regular hourly wage. The overtime rate (time and one-half) will be paid for those hours that are actually worked in a pay period and will not include sick or vacation time. Holiday pay shall be calculated as hours worked for purposes of overtime pay.

- B. All overtime must be requested by the department head. Under no circumstances will overtime wages be paid unless the employee has been requested, and given prior approval, to work the overtime hours.
title: § 56-7.4. Overtime pay.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VII. Conditions of Employment > § 56-7.5. Compensatory time.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VII. Conditions of Employment > § 56-7.5. Compensatory time.

- A. Nonexempt employees shall be eligible to accumulate up to 40 hours of compensatory time. "Compensatory time" is defined as paid time off in the future in lieu of an immediate cash payment at the overtime rate for time worked in excess of 40 hours in a pay period. The employee must request the award of future compensatory time prior to the closing of the payroll date in which the overtime hours were worked. Paid compensatory time shall be at the rate of time and one-half for all overtime hours (e.g., 10 hours of overtime translates into 15 hours of paid compensatory time off). The employee may replenish used compensatory time up to the maximum amount of 40 hours. Any accumulated compensatory time will be used before accumulated vacation time.

- B. The employee must receive the department head's or his/her designee's prior approval before using accumulated compensatory time. Employees may carry forward up to 20 hours of compensatory time each July 1. All unused compensatory time over the 20 hours will be paid in the dollar equivalent of unused compensatory time prior to June 30 of each year. At all times, it is incumbent upon the employee to make a timely request for prior approval of the use of compensatory time.
title: § 56-7.5. Compensatory time.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VII. Conditions of Employment > § 56-7.6. Absenteeism.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VII. Conditions of Employment > § 56-7.6. Absenteeism.

Employees who have not reported to work for a period of three days or more, and who are not on an approved leave, shall be considered to have voluntarily resigned from their position and will be terminated from said position. Exceptions to this policy may be made by the City Manager, based upon the results of an investigation.
title: § 56-7.6. Absenteeism.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VII. Conditions of Employment > § 56-7.7. Outside employment.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VII. Conditions of Employment > § 56-7.7. Outside employment.

Regular, full-time employment with the City is considered the individual's primary employment. Employees may not engage in other employment that interferes with or otherwise creates a conflict of interest with the performance of assigned duties. Whenever it appears that any such outside employment may constitute a conflict of interest, the employee is expected to consult with his or her department head, who may consult with the City Manager or City Solicitor.
title: § 56-7.7. Outside employment.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VII. Conditions of Employment > § 56-7.8. Inclement weather.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VII. Conditions of Employment > § 56-7.8. Inclement weather.

During periods of inclement weather, when conditions begin to reach the stage where travel may become hazardous, the City Manager may deem it appropriate to keep nonessential, administrative employees home for their own safety or release employees from work early. During such closings, department heads and professional staff may be considered essential for purposes of maintaining City operations. The City Manager may deem it appropriate to close early due to inclement weather. Office closings shall be posted in as many places as possible, including Facebook, local news stations, website, etc.
title: § 56-7.8. Inclement weather.

article: Article VIII. Employee Training and Development
breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VIII. Employee Training and Development > § 56-8.1. Policy.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VIII. Employee Training and Development > § 56-8.1. Policy.

*[Amended 5-20-2025 by Ord. No. 101-2025]*

It is the policy of the City to encourage and assist in the professional development of all employees when such assistance is in the best interest of the City. The purpose of this policy shall be to foster or promote the training and development of employees, improve the quality of service to the City, equip employees for career development within the City, and provide a reservoir of occupational skills necessary to meet current and future employment needs. Regular, full-time employees are eligible for the training and tuition reimbursement benefits as described below. During their probationary period, employees are not eligible for course reimbursement until their probationary period has ended.
title: § 56-8.1. Policy.

article: Article VIII. Employee Training and Development
breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VIII. Employee Training and Development > § 56-8.2. City-initiated training.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VIII. Employee Training and Development > § 56-8.2. City-initiated training.

Seminars, certificate courses and in-house training workshops will be considered as City-initiated training to provide all employees with training sufficient to keep them current with practices in their respective disciplines. City-initiated training expenses will be paid for out of the employee's department training budget. Employees shall not be paid or receive compensatory time when attending courses, conferences or seminars during after-duty hours.
title: § 56-8.2. City-initiated training.

article: Article VIII. Employee Training and Development
breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VIII. Employee Training and Development > § 56-8.3. Conferences and workshops.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VIII. Employee Training and Development > § 56-8.3. Conferences and workshops.

*[Amended 5-20-2025 by Ord. No. 101-2025]*

Requests to attend courses, conferences, workshops and seminars shall be made as part of the budgetary process. City payment for attendance at these courses, conferences, workshops and seminars will be based on the direct value to the employee and City, budgetary constraints and applicability to current municipal affairs. Employees shall not be paid or receive compensatory time when attending courses, conferences, workshops or seminars during after-duty hours.
title: § 56-8.3. Conferences and workshops.

article: Article VIII. Employee Training and Development
breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VIII. Employee Training and Development > § 56-8.4. Employee-initiated training.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VIII. Employee Training and Development > § 56-8.4. Employee-initiated training.

*[Amended 5-20-2025 by Ord. No. 101-2025]*

- A. Employees may elect courses or programs to further their education or professional development. Credit-hour courses in a degree program will be considered employee-initiated and will be paid out of the personnel training budget. The number of employees allowed to participate per semester will depend on the funds available.

- B. Course/Tuition reimbursement requires preapproval, with preference given to employees taking courses that relate directly to their current positions and remaining funds to employees taking courses to improve skills for career advancement purposes.

- C. In order for more employees to be eligible for tuition reimbursement, the City will reimburse an employee up to the amount listed below per class:

  - (1) Undergraduate class: $600.

  - (2) Graduate class: $1,000.

- D. Employees will be reimbursed for preapproved courses upon successful completion of the course(s) according to the following schedule and grade received:

  - (1) A: 100% of the tuition rate.

  - (2) B: 75% of the tuition rate.

  - (3) C: 50% of the tuition rate.

  - (4) D, E, F, Incomplete: 0% of the tuition rate.

- E. Textbooks and all other expenses are the responsibility of the employee.

- F. Employees receiving tuition/course reimbursement agree to reimburse the City for tuition costs if the employee does not remain in the employ of the City for a period of one year following the last completed course or block of training.

- G. Requests for course/tuition reimbursement shall be submitted on the "Pre-Approved Tuition Request and Tuition Reimbursement Request" form prior to enrolling to ensure adequate funding is available. The form outlines the procedure for making requests and receiving reimbursement(s).
title: § 56-8.4. Employee-initiated training.

article: Article VIII. Employee Training and Development
breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VIII. Employee Training and Development > § 56-8.5. Hours worked.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article VIII. Employee Training and Development > § 56-8.5. Hours worked.

An employee that is attending preapproved training during a normally scheduled work day will be paid the employee's regular work hours for the day. If an overnight stay is required, no overtime will be paid for those hours while attending the training session.
title: § 56-8.5. Hours worked.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article IX. Discipline > § 56-9.1. Discipline policy.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article IX. Discipline > § 56-9.1. Discipline policy.

*[Amended 5-20-2025 by Ord. No. 101-2025]*

- A. This policy follows the principles of progressive discipline. The progressive discipline steps are as follows:

  - (1) Oral warning (put in writing for file purpose).

  - (2) Written warning.

  - (3) Suspension.

  - (4) Demotion and/or dismissal.

- B. In less serious cases, employee discipline will begin with oral warning. In more serious cases, the discipline process may begin at written reprimand, suspension, demotion or dismissal.

- C. Nothing in these rules shall limit the City's right to suspend or discharge an employee during the employee's probationary period with or without cause.

- D. All nonprobationary employees may grieve disciplinary actions through the grievance procedure. These rules do not limit the right of the City to discharge employees for nondisciplinary reasons, including, but not limited to, lack of work, elimination of positions, reduction in force or budget constraints.

- E. All disciplinary actions shall be documented in writing and reviewed with the employee. Copies shall be forwarded to the Human Resource Officer for placement in the employee's personnel file.
title: § 56-9.1. Discipline policy.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article IX. Discipline > § 56-9.2. Causes for disciplinary action.
title: § 56-9.2. Causes for disciplinary action.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article IX. Discipline > § 56-9.3. Political activities.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article IX. Discipline > § 56-9.3. Political activities.

- A. No employee shall participate in any political activity which would be in conflict or incompatible with the performance of his/her official duties with the City.

- B. Under the provisions of the Hatch Act, which applies to entities receiving federal funds, City employees are not prevented from enrolling in political or party organizations, expressing political views, campaigning for or against issues, signing nominating papers or voting in all elections, caucuses and primaries with complete freedom.

- C. Under provisions of the Hatch Act, employees are prohibited from using their authority or influence to interfere with an election, may not solicit or discourage political activity of any person who has business before the City and may not engage in political activity while on duty.

- D. Employees wishing additional information are advised to contact the City Clerk, City Manager or the City Solicitor.
title: § 56-9.3. Political activities.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article IX. Discipline > § 56-9.4. Standards of conduct; social media.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article IX. Discipline > § 56-9.4. Standards of conduct; social media.

- A. Standard of conduct. No official or employee of the City shall solicit or receive any pay, commission, money or thing of value, or derive any benefit, profit or advantage, directly or indirectly, from or by reason of any improvement, alteration or repair required by authority of the City, or any contract to which the City shall be a party, except compensation or salary as established for such official or employee. A violation of any of the provisions of this section, or any established common law doctrines or statutory provisions under the State of Maine, shall disqualify the offender to continue in the office or employment of the City, and the official or employee shall be removed therefrom. Any contract in which an official or employee of the City is directly or indirectly interested shall become absolutely void, and any money which shall have been paid on such contract by the City may be recovered back from any or all the persons interested therein, by joint or several action. Gifts do not include advertising items or items of nominal value such as calendars, pens, pencils, fruit baskets, etc.

- B. Use of public property. No official or employee shall request or permit the use of City-owned vehicles, equipment, materials or property for personal convenience or profit, except when such vehicles, equipment, materials or property are available to the public generally or are provided as a municipal policy for the use of such official or employee in the conduct of official business.

- C. Social media. In use the use of personal social media, employees shall not:

  - (1) Share proprietary or classified information;

  - (2) Violate City policies;

  - (3) Use the City seal, logo or images; and

  - (4) Purport to represent the City.
title: § 56-9.4. Standards of conduct; social media.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article X. Grievance Procedure > § 56-10.1. General policy.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article X. Grievance Procedure > § 56-10.1. General policy.

- A. The City's grievance procedure is intended to provide an opportunity for employees to bring concerns, complaints and other grievance situations to the attention of management.

- B. While the City desires that grievances be addressed informally, it is recognized that there will be matters that may be resolved only after appeal and subsequent review. The City will deal promptly with employee complaints or grievances concerning interpretation or application of this Personnel Ordinance.
title: § 56-10.1. General policy.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article X. Grievance Procedure > § 56-10.2. Informal resolution.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article X. Grievance Procedure > § 56-10.2. Informal resolution.

Employees should attempt to resolve disputes through discussion with their immediate supervisor or department head. If the grievance is not resolved informally, the employee should use the procedure as outlined in § 56-10.3. The Human Resource Officer is available to assist in resolving disputes at the request of any of the individuals involved. If the matter is not resolved during the informal process, the employee may appeal utilizing § 56-10.3 of the grievance procedure.
title: § 56-10.2. Informal resolution.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article X. Grievance Procedure > § 56-10.3. Grievance procedure.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article X. Grievance Procedure > § 56-10.3. Grievance procedure.

A grievance must be filed, in writing, within five working days of the event being grieved. To ensure a prompt and fair review, the following steps are provided:

- A. If the employee is not satisfied with informal discussions with his/her supervisor or department head, in accordance with § 56-10.2, the employee shall submit the grievance in writing to the department head, with a copy to the Human Resource Officer. The department head will schedule a meeting with the employee within five working days after receipt of the written grievance. The department head shall attempt to resolve the matter and shall respond, in writing, within five working days, providing a copy of the written response to the Human Resource Officer.

- B. If the matter is not resolved by the department head, the employee may appeal the grievance in writing, within five working days, to the City Manager, or his/her designee. The City Manager (or designee) shall meet with the employee within five working days and shall provide a written decision within five working days of the meeting. The time lines may be extended upon the written request and mutual agreement of the parties.
title: § 56-10.3. Grievance procedure.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article XI. Resignation and Separation > § 56-11.1. Separation policy.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article XI. Resignation and Separation > § 56-11.1. Separation policy.

Prior to separation from City service, employees may schedule a meeting with a representative in the Human Resources Office to discuss various options relative to benefits or other conversion privileges available to the employee. At this time, appropriate steps will be taken to provide for the payment of all leave entitlements in the final paycheck. Separating employees shall turn in all City-owned property in their possession and shall leave a forwarding address with the department head or in the Human Resources Office for purposes of forwarding final check, IRS forms, etc.
title: § 56-11.1. Separation policy.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article XI. Resignation and Separation > § 56-11.2. Types of separation.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article XI. Resignation and Separation > § 56-11.2. Types of separation.

- A. Resignation. Resignations from City service shall be submitted, in writing, to the department head at least 14 days in advance. The resignation shall be forwarded to the Human Resource Officer, with a copy to the City Manager. The effective date of the resignation will be at the close of business on the date specified in the resignation that coincides with the last day worked. The last day worked shall be the official termination date for calculating all payroll and vacation benefits.

- B. Layoff. "Layoff" shall mean involuntary separation of an employee because of lack of work, lack of funds or abolishment of the position without any fault on the part of the employee. Employees with the shortest length of continuous service within the same classification in the affected department will be laid off first, provided merit and ability to perform the job are equal within the classification.

- C. Dismissal. An employee may be removed at any time during the probationary period or for cause as outlined in Article IX.

- D. Suspension. An employee may be suspended from his/her position for cause. A suspended employee is still an incumbent in the position. The interruption from duty is a temporary, disciplinary measure and may be with or without pay. An employee who is suspended without pay for more than three weeks shall be responsible for the full monthly cost of their insurance benefits.

- E. Disability. Employees may be separated from work due to a disability whereby he or she is unable to perform duties of the job. The City will consider all provisions of the Americans with Disabilities Act.

- F. Retirement. Employees hired prior to January 1, 1986, with 25 years of continuous service may choose to retire from City service upon reaching the age of 65, or at age 60 and 30 years of service. Said employees will receive the monetary value (or early retirement) for the full amount (or time) of their accumulated sick leave, up to the maximum of 120 days. Employees will have the monetary value of their sick leave benefit reduced by 4% for each year under age 65. (See § 56-6.4A.)

- G. Death.

  - (1) Upon death, all compensation due to the employee under the provisions of these policies shall be paid to the employee's estate and/or beneficiaries pursuant to IRS rules.

  - (2) In the event of the death of an employee hired prior to January 1, 1986, the employee's estate shall receive a portion of sick leave benefits according to Subsection F above.
title: § 56-11.2. Types of separation.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article XII. Miscellaneous Provisions > § 56-12.1. Personnel files.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article XII. Miscellaneous Provisions > § 56-12.1. Personnel files.

Employees, upon request, may be permitted to review their personnel files. Such review shall be arranged with the Human Resource Officer and conducted during normal office hours. Upon written request, an employee shall be provided a copy of any or all materials in his/her personnel files, provided that such copies shall be provided at the employee's expense if the copies number more than 10.
title: § 56-12.1. Personnel files.

breadcrumb: Chapter 56. Personnel > Article XII. Miscellaneous Provisions > § 56-12.2. Service awards.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 56. Personnel > Article XII. Miscellaneous Provisions > § 56-12.2. Service awards.

The City of Waterville shall recognize employees who have completed years of continuous service with a service award. The awards will be presented in five-year increments at 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, etc. during the annual Employee Recognition Dinner.
title: § 56-12.2. Service awards.

title: Chapter 61. Purchasing (history and notes)

breadcrumb: Chapter 61. Purchasing > § 61-1. Purpose and policy.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 61. Purchasing > § 61-1. Purpose and policy.

As provided for in the City Charter, Article VII, Section 5, the purpose of this chapter is to provide procedures for the purchase or lease of equipment, supplies or services for the City of Waterville. The current policy of the City is to maintain a decentralized purchasing process which shall be monitored by the City Manager and Finance Director.
title: § 61-1. Purpose and policy.

breadcrumb: Chapter 61. Purchasing > § 61-2. Purchases or leases of $20,000 or less.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 61. Purchasing > § 61-2. Purchases or leases of $20,000 or less.

- A. Department directors are authorized to approve purchases of equipment, supplies or services of $20,000 or less in value, provided such purchases have been approved by the City Manager and are part of the department's annual budget appropriation. In addition, department directors are responsible for the following:

  - (1) To make every effort to secure the best possible price for all purchases or leases of $20,000 or less. This may involve an informal bidding process when, in the opinion of the City Manager or the department director, there are multiple vendors for that particular product or service.

  - (2) To plan future purchases to provide ample time to secure favorable prices.

  - (3) To assure that a sufficient unencumbered balance remains in the department's appropriation before a purchase is made.

  - (4) To advise and obtain approval from the City Manager for any purchase necessary for the continued operation of the department, which purchase may not have been approved in the annual appropriation or which purchase may exceed the department's total available funds.

- B. The City Manager shall ensure that the requirements of this chapter are not circumvented by multiple or separate purchases of $20,000 or less to avoid the bid requirements as outlined below.
section_title: Purchases or leases of $20,000 or less.
title: § 61-2. Purchases or leases of $20,000 or less.

breadcrumb: Chapter 61. Purchasing > § 61-3. Purchases or leases in excess of $20,000.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 61. Purchasing > § 61-3. Purchases or leases in excess of $20,000.

- A. All purchases or leases in excess of $20,000 shall require a competitive bid process which is subject to review and approval by the City Council. Lease proposals with multiple-year payment terms shall indicate both the annual payment and total lease cost. This requirement shall not apply to the services of expert witnesses to be employed by the City in present or anticipated legal action.

- B. The following procedures shall be followed for all purchases and leases in excess of $20,000:

  - (1) In addition to notification to all known and interested vendors, the City shall publish a notice on the City's official website no later than five days before the bid deadline.

  - (2) The City Manager and/or the department director shall make every effort to ensure that at least three responsible bidders have been contacted for each purchase.

  - (3) All bids shall be submitted in a clearly marked, sealed envelope and opened in public at the hour stated in the notice.

  - (4) All original bids, together with all documents pertaining to the award of the contract, shall be retained and made a part of the permanent file or record and shall be open to public inspection upon request.

  - (5) All purchases and leases in excess of $20,000 require a purchase requisition and a copy of the signed resolution or order approved by Council prior to submittal to the Finance Office for payment.

  - (6) Items such as solid waste tipping fees, insurance costs, fuel purchase and other similar operational expenses approved by the Council as part of the annual budget process shall be exempt from the requirements of this section.

  - (7) If a purchase/project requires multiple payments, each invoice submitted for payment, after the original, must clearly reference the approved purchase order number and the approved Council resolution or order number or the invoice will be returned without payment.
section_title: Purchases or leases in excess of $20,000.
title: § 61-3. Purchases or leases in excess of $20,000.

breadcrumb: Chapter 61. Purchasing > § 61-4. Bid review, approval or rejection.

breadcrumb: Chapter 61. Purchasing > § 61-5. Waiver of bid process.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 61. Purchasing > § 61-5. Waiver of bid process.

- A. Notwithstanding the foregoing requirements of § 61-4, the bid process may be waived under one or more of the following conditions:

  - (1) Price has been determined by a current and still valid bid process conducted by a recognized operating division of the state or county governments or the City Board of Education or a joint group composed of municipalities or quasi-municipal entities.

  - (2) When the Council is provided with factual data submitted by the administration that the price under consideration is the best available price and that, due to circumstances beyond the control of the administration, there is an insufficient time to resort to the normal bid process.

  - (3) When the Council is provided with factual data submitted by the administration that the matter under consideration is unique, noncompetitive or with a current vendor that has a contract with the City for specific goods/services.

  - (4) The Council may extend a contract for goods/services when it determines that it is in the best interest of the City to do so. Said extension shall be for no more than two years and will require a positive report from the administration that the contractor/vendor has met all contractual obligations and that there are important reasons to continue the relationship.

  - (5) When projects are entirely funded with privately raised funds.

- B. To waive the bid process, the City Council must determine by a two-thirds majority of the Council members present that Subsection A(1), (2), (3), (4) or (5) above exists.

content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 103. Adult Businesses

*[HISTORY: Adopted by the City Council of the City of Waterville effective 3-17-2011 by Ord. No. 11-2011. Amendments noted where applicable.]*
history: [HISTORY: Adopted by the City Council of the City of Waterville effective 3-17-2011 by Ord. No. 11-2011. Amendments noted where applicable.]
title: Chapter 103. Adult Businesses (history and notes)

breadcrumb: Chapter 103. Adult Businesses > § 103-1. Definitions.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 103. Adult Businesses > § 103-1. Definitions.

*[Amended 5-20-2025 by Ord. No. 101-2025]*

As used in this chapter, the following terms shall have the meanings indicated:

**ADULT BUSINESS ESTABLISHMENT**: Any retail business, whether conducted from a fixed or mobile location or vehicle, including, but not limited to, any bookstore, newsstand, novelty store, nightclub, bar, cabaret, amusement arcade, spa, massage parlor or theater, which:

  - A. Keeps for public patronage or permits or allows the operation or use of any adult amusement device containing sexually explicit material; or

  - B. Permits any person on the premises, including an employee, entertainer or patron, to expose that person's genitals, pubic hair, buttocks or perineum, or the areola of a female breast, to a patron or member of the general public;

  - C. Exhibits or displays, more often than an average of one week during any calendar month of operation, any motion pictures or any other visual representation described or advertised as being "X-rated" or "for adults only," or which customarily excludes persons from any portion of the premises by reason of immaturity of age by the use of such or similar phrases; or

  - D. Has a substantial portion of its stock-in-trade that consists of products containing sexually explicit material;

  - E. Is an establishment or place primarily in the business of providing:

    - (1) A steam bath or sauna;

    - (2) Other bathing or hot tub services; or

    - (3) "Rubdown" or other massage services by a person or persons not licensed or exempt from licensing under state law.

**SEXUALLY EXPLICIT**: The display or depiction of sex organs during actual or simulated sexual intercourse or sexual acts as defined in 17-A M.R.S. § 251.
title: § 103-1. Definitions.

breadcrumb: Chapter 103. Adult Businesses > § 103-2. Findings and purpose.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 103. Adult Businesses > § 103-2. Findings and purpose.

The Council hereby finds that because of their unique and potentially offensive nature, adult business establishments can have a blighting influence on the surrounding neighborhood if permitted in certain districts or if allowed to concentrate in certain other districts within the City. Moreover, such establishments are incompatible with uses characterized by family and youth-related activities. The purpose of this chapter is, therefore, to prevent such deleterious effects and, thus, protect public health, safety and general welfare by regulating the location and certain other aspects of adult business establishments.
title: § 103-2. Findings and purpose.

breadcrumb: Chapter 103. Adult Businesses > § 103-3. Location and visibility restrictions.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 103. Adult Businesses > § 103-3. Location and visibility restrictions.

- A. Adult business establishments shall be at least 1,000 feet from any other adult business establishment, at least 250 feet from the nearest property line of any public, private or parochial school, church, synagogue or similar place of worship, public library, playground or child-care facility, and at least 250 feet from any Residential District (R-A, R-B, R-C, R-D and R-R) as measured in a straight line without regard to intervening structures or objects. They also cannot be located between Union Street and Sherwin Street and between Elm Street and the Kennebec River.

- B. No sexually explicit materials, entertainment or activity shall be visible from the exterior of the premises.
title: § 103-3. Location and visibility restrictions.

breadcrumb: Chapter 103. Adult Businesses > § 103-4. Violations and penalties.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 103. Adult Businesses > § 103-4. Violations and penalties.

Violations of this chapter are subject to the civil penalties, injunctive remedies and attorney's fees provisions of 30-A M.R.S. § 4452(3), as amended. Each day a violation continues is a separate violation.
title: § 103-4. Violations and penalties.

content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 109. Airport > Article I. Administration > § 109-1. Airport Manager.

- A. The City, through its City Manager, will appoint a person to act as the Airport Manager.

- B. Responsibilities of this position will vary according to whether or not the City has a fixed-based operator (FBO) stationed at the airport. At a minimum, the Airport Manager will be responsible for all operational and planning needs of the airport. This could include the supervision of personnel, the purchase of equipment and supplies, preparation of the annual budget and planning for capital improvement projects.

- C. In addition, this person will be the contact person for all state and federal regulatory agencies on matters pertaining to the airport.

article: Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations
breadcrumb: Chapter 109. Airport > Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations > § 109-3. Purpose.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 109. Airport > Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations > § 109-3. Purpose.

The purpose of this article is to promote public safety and to establish aircraft taxi and vehicle speed limits on the appropriate portions of the airport.
title: § 109-3. Purpose.

article: Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations
breadcrumb: Chapter 109. Airport > Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations > § 109-4. Aircraft taxi speeds.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 109. Airport > Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations > § 109-4. Aircraft taxi speeds.

Aircraft taxi speeds shall not exceed 20 miles per hour on the ramps and taxiways of said airport. Taxi tests, where speeds exceeding 20 miles per hour may be necessary, shall be conducted on the runways after receiving prior permission from the Airport Manager or his authorized representative.
title: § 109-4. Aircraft taxi speeds.

article: Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations
breadcrumb: Chapter 109. Airport > Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations > § 109-5. Speed of vehicles.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 109. Airport > Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations > § 109-5. Speed of vehicles.

- A. The speed limits on the airport proper, taxiways, ramps, etc. shall be 15 miles per hour.

- B. There is no attempt to establish speed limits on the runway proper; however, vehicles operating on the runway shall be operated at safe and reasonable speeds.
title: § 109-5. Speed of vehicles.

article: Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations
breadcrumb: Chapter 109. Airport > Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations > § 109-6. Operation of vehicles on ramps, taxiways, runways.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 109. Airport > Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations > § 109-6. Operation of vehicles on ramps, taxiways, runways.

- A. No vehicles, including motorized recreation vehicles and motorized terrain vehicles, shall operate on the ramps, taxiways, runways or any other portions of the airport proper without the permission of the Airport Manager or his authorized representative.

- B. Vehicles must have their headlights on while operating in the areas designated in this section.
section_title: Operation of vehicles on ramps, taxiways, runways.
title: § 109-6. Operation of vehicles on ramps, taxiways, runways.

article: Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations
breadcrumb: Chapter 109. Airport > Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations > § 109-7. Takeoffs and landings.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 109. Airport > Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations > § 109-7. Takeoffs and landings.

The entire airport or designated runways may be closed by the Airport Manager during inclement weather conditions or for other reasons. All regulations published by the Federal Aviation Administration shall apply during such times.
title: § 109-7. Takeoffs and landings.

article: Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations
breadcrumb: Chapter 109. Airport > Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations > § 109-8. Calm wind runway.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 109. Airport > Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations > § 109-8. Calm wind runway.

- A. Runway "5-23" is designated as the calm wind runway. Runway "5-23" shall be used by all arriving and/or departing aircraft whenever the surface wind is less than five nautical miles per hour.

- B. Any pilot who deviates from this procedure shall yield to conflicting traffic which is conforming to this section, and remain clear of the traffic pattern or runway until the way is clear. The intent is to not disrupt aircraft operations conforming to the calm wind runway procedure.

- C. In the event of an emergency, the pilot may elect to use any runway and claim priority by broadcasting the appropriate radio signal or phrase.
title: § 109-8. Calm wind runway.

article: Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations
breadcrumb: Chapter 109. Airport > Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations > § 109-9. Animals prohibited.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 109. Airport > Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations > § 109-9. Animals prohibited.

Animals shall not be permitted to roam freely on the airport proper. Any animal which is observed on the runways, taxiways, ramps or grassy areas shall be apprehended. Any costs incurred shall be the responsibility of the owner of the animal or animals.
title: § 109-9. Animals prohibited.

article: Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations
breadcrumb: Chapter 109. Airport > Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations > § 109-10. Pedestrian traffic.
content:
City of Waterville, ME Code
Chapter 109. Airport > Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations > § 109-10. Pedestrian traffic.

Pedestrian traffic shall not be permitted on the ramps, or taxiways, or within 500 feet of the runways, without the permission of the Airport Manager or his authorized representative.
title: § 109-10. Pedestrian traffic.

content:

The Airport Manager or his authorized representative shall be responsible for directing all aircraft to suitable parking spaces.
title: § 109-11. Parking of aircraft.

content:

Aircraft operational tests or engine run-ups shall be made in the designated areas. In no case will these tests or engine run-ups be performed in the vicinity of the terminal building, any hangar or other inhabited structures.

Chapter 109. Airport > Article II. Safety Rules and Regulations > § 109-13. Restriction of use of ramps, taxiways or runways.

The Airport Manager, or his authorized representative, shall have the authority to restrict the use of any ramps, taxiways or runways to any person whom he deems to be incapable of safely operating on these areas.

The Airport Manager or his authorized representative shall notify the City Manager of any accident which occurs at the airport, or its vicinity, as soon as practicable. A follow-up written report shall be rendered within 72 hours.
